tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Price tiers, review-filter multipliers, quantity limits and what a delivered list contains. Call this before quoting if the person wants to compare options.

tools.name: quote_lead_list
tools.description: Exact price for a lead list: business types, locations, quantity and optional minimum-review bar. Returns the amount the site charges, what is included and delivery terms. Nothing is created.

tools.name: get_sample_leads
tools.description: A few illustrative rows in the exact delivered format (placeholder businesses on reserved example domains, not real leads), plus the column reference.

tools.name: get_checkout_link
tools.description: A leadproof.co link with the list already configured. The person opens it, reviews the price and pays on the site. Use this when they prefer to finish in a browser. Nothing is created until they order.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Creates the order and returns a PayPal approval link. The PERSON must open the link and approve the payment; nothing is charged until they do. Ask for the delivery email first: the CSV and the order page go there. Returns the order id, the approval link, an order-status link and a status token for g

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Status of an order created with create_order: awaiting approval, in review, building, delivered (with a download link) or refunded. Needs the order_id and status_token that create_order returned.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_pricing, quote_lead_list, get_checkout_link, create_order, get_order_status · Private data: create_order · Public sink: create_order · Destructive: get_sample_leads.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_pricing, quote_lead_list, get_checkout_link, create_order, get_order_status · Private data: create_order · Public sink: create_order · Destructive: get_sample_leads

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
